1.

Sri Roopesh Srivastava, Advocate has filed memo of appearance on behalf of opposite party no.2 (first informant) today in court, which is taken on record.
2.
Office is directed to print the name of Sri Roopesh Srivastava, as counsel for the opposite party.

3. Heard learned counsel for the appellant, learned AGA for the state respondent no. 1 and Sri Roopesh Srivastava, opposite party no.2 (first informant).
4.

This is a criminal appeal under Section 14-A (2) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (SC/ST) Act assailing the order dated 31.5.2025 whereby Criminal Misc. 2nd Bail Application No. 2579 of 2025 (Amit Yadav Vs. State of U.P.) in Case Crime Amit Yadav vs State Of U.P. And Another on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53864333/
1 No.31 of 2024, under Section 376 IPC and Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST Act, PS Gorakhnath, District - Gorakhpur, moved on behalf of the appellant (accused) has been rejected.

sentences.text: As per the FIR version, on 24.1.2024 at about 1:30 pm, while she was going for excretion from her room, she was gagged and taken away by the accused and forcibly sexually assaulted.
5. It is submitted that during the trial, the prosecutrix had appeared as PW1 and unequivocally denied any such incident as averred in the FIR.
Even in the cross-examination, she has denied the incident of forceful sexual assault and the hurling caste related filthy language upon her.
It is next submitted that the learned trial court, while rejecting the second bail application, has miserably failed to consider the deposition made on behalf of the prosecutrix before the court.
In view of the testimony of the PW1, the present appellant (accused) is liable to be enlarged on bail.

6. Learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 (prosecutrix) has nodded the submissions as advanced by learned counsel for the appellant (accused) and contended thatopposite party no. 2 has unequivocally denied the complicity of the present appellant in commission of any such crime as mentioned in the FIR.

7. Having considered the submissions advanced by the learned counsel for the parties and upon perusal of the record, it is manifest that the first bail application, moved on behalf of the accused,
has been rejected by order dated 14.03.2024.
Criminal Appeal No. 3224 of 2024, arising out of same bail application rejected on 14.3.2024, has been dismissed as well vide order dated 10.01.2025 passed by a co-ordinate bench of this court.

At the subsequent stage, while PW1 has made the statement denying the complicity of the present appellant in the commission of crime as mentioned in the FIR which was intact in cross-examination as well, the second bail application has been moved, being 2nd Bail Application No. 2579 of 2025.

The learned trial court has rejected the aforesaid bail application, vide order dated 31.05.2025, with an observation that the previous bail application was rejected on merits and same had been affirmed by the Hon'ble High court in appeal arising out of the rejection of the said bail application.

Despite the fact that the statement of the PW1 was on record which has been pressed by the appellant before the trial court, the trial court has illegally evaded said statement and was influenced with the rejection of the previous bail application on merits, which had been affirmed up to the Hon'ble High Court.

8. The testimony of PW1 has been filed as Annexure no. 5 to the paper book of the instant appeal,
wherein the prosecutrix has unequivocally stated that her statement under section 164 Cr.P.C. was made under undue pressure and coercion, however, now she is making statement on her own volition denying the complicity of the present appellant in the commission of any such crime as mentioned in the F.I.R.
No forceful sexual assault has been committed and caste related abusive language has been hurled by the appellant.
She has admitted her signature and the photographs pasted on her statement under Section 164 (Paper No.17 Ka) of Cr.P.C. which has been marked as Ext. 2.
Even in her cross-examination, she has unequivocally accepted her examination-in-chief.

In view of the subsequent event, wherein prosecutrix has denied the complicity of the present appellant in the commission of crime in her testimony being PW1 before the trial court, the involvement of the present appellant in the commission of crime is prima facie doubtful.

The learned trial court has declared the prosecutrix (victim) hostile on 17.5.2025, which is evident from the statement of PW 1 Amit Yadav vs State Of U.P. And Another on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53864333/
2 (page no.46 of the memo of book).
9.

sentences.text: In view of the above, I do not have any hesitation to enlarge the present appellant on bail.
As such, instant criminal appeal succeeds and is hereby allowed.

The order impugned dated 31.5.2025 passed by the Special Judge (SC/ST Act), Gorakhpur, in Case Crime No.31 of 2024 under Section 376 IPC and Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST Act, P.S. - Gorakhnath, District - Gorakhpur, is hereby quashed.

10. Resultantly, present appellant, namely, Amit Yadav is enlarged on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties of equal amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned in Case Crime No.31 of 2024 under Section 376 IPC and Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST Act, P.S. - Gorakhnath, District - Gorakhpur, under the following conditions :
(i) The appellant shall not misuse the liberty of bail in any manner whatsoever.
(ii) The appellant shall pursue the case regularly, shall not seek unnecessary adjournments and shall co-operate in early disposal of the trial.
